channel.title: Tech World Window
channel.description: Your Window Into Technology — Windows, PC gaming and hardware guides.

item.title: Windows Troubleshooting: A Complete Guide to Diagnosing and Fixing Windows Problems
item.description: A universal, evidence-led framework for Windows 11 and Windows 10: find the failing layer first, then fix startup failures, blue screens, freezes, slow performance, updates, drivers, networking, apps, and hardware faults without making things worse.

item.title: Windows 11 Won’t Start: A Safe Troubleshooting Guide
item.description: Windows can fail before sign-in, hang on the logo, loop through recovery, or show a blank screen. Identify the stage first, then choose the least destructive fix.

item.title: Windows Update Stuck? How Long to Wait, What to Check, and How to Fix It (Windows 11 & 10)
item.description: Windows 11 or 10 update stuck at 0%, 30%, 99% or ‘Working on updates’? Learn how long to wait, how to tell slow from frozen, and fix it step by step without losing data.

item.title: Windows 11 High Memory Usage: How to Find the Real Cause
item.description: High RAM usage is not automatically a fault. Learn how to distinguish normal caching from a runaway application, memory pressure, or a genuine memory problem.

item.title: Windows 11 Unknown Device in Device Manager: Find the Driver with the Hardware ID
item.description: An Unknown Device entry usually means Windows lacks the right driver or cannot identify the hardware correctly. Identify the hardware before downloading a random driver.

item.title: Windows 11 100% Disk Usage: What It Means and What to Check
item.description: 100% disk usage can mean a busy workload, a slow drive, paging, background maintenance, or storage trouble. Identify which process is responsible before applying generic fixes.

item.title: Windows 11 Slow Startup: Find Out What Is Delaying Sign-In
item.description: A slow boot can be caused by startup applications, storage delays, updates, drivers, or firmware. Measure where the delay happens before disabling services.

item.title: Low FPS in PC Games: How to Find the Real Bottleneck
item.description: Low FPS can come from the GPU, CPU, memory, thermals, settings, background tasks, or the game engine. Use frame rate and frame-time evidence instead of guessing.

item.title: PC Games Keep Crashing to Desktop: A Step-by-Step Diagnosis
item.description: Game crashes can come from drivers, corrupted files, unstable hardware settings, overlays, memory, or the game itself. Narrow the cause before reinstalling everything.

item.title: GPU at 100% Usage While Gaming: Is That a Problem?
item.description: A GPU running near 100% during a game is often normal and can mean the graphics card is being used efficiently. The surrounding temperature, clock, FPS, and symptoms matter.

item.title: How Much RAM Do You Need for Gaming and Windows?
item.description: More RAM is useful when your workload is actually memory-constrained. Compare 16GB, 32GB, and 64GB against the games and applications you run instead of treating capacity as a universal speed upgrade.

item.title: GPU Overheating While Gaming: What to Check Before Replacing It
item.description: High GPU temperatures can come from airflow, dust, fan behavior, room temperature, a demanding workload, or degraded cooling. Diagnose the cause before buying a new graphics card.

item.title: PC Power Supply Problems: Symptoms That Point to the PSU
item.description: Random restarts, shutdowns, failed startups, and instability can involve the power supply, but software and other hardware can look similar. Use symptoms and controlled tests to narrow it down.

item.title: SSD Nearly Full: How Much Free Space Does Windows Need?
item.description: A nearly full SSD can leave too little working space for Windows, updates, applications, and temporary data. Learn what to clean and when a larger drive makes sense.

item.title: DDR4 vs DDR5 RAM: What Actually Changes?
item.description: DDR4 and DDR5 are different memory generations with different platform support, speeds, module behavior, and upgrade paths. They are not interchangeable on a typical motherboard.

item.title: Laptop NVMe SSD Upgrade: Check Compatibility Before You Buy
item.description: A laptop can have an M.2 slot and still reject a particular SSD because of interface, size, keying, firmware, thermal, or capacity constraints. Check the platform first.

item.title: Can You Upgrade a Gaming Laptop? Check RAM and SSD First
item.description: Some gaming laptops allow both RAM and SSD upgrades, some allow only storage, and some use soldered memory. Check the exact model before assuming it is upgradeable.

item.title: What Really Changes When an SSD Gets Nearly Full?
item.description: A practical TWW investigation into free space, Windows storage behavior, sustained workloads, and what evidence actually points to an SSD becoming the bottleneck.

item.title: Windows Shows 100% Disk Usage but Very Low MB/s: What Is Actually Happening?
item.description: Why Task Manager can show 100% disk active time while transfer speed remains low, and how to diagnose latency, queueing, background I/O and storage faults.

item.title: What Actually Causes PC Game Stuttering? A Frame-Time Investigation
item.description: A TWW framework for separating shader compilation, CPU limits, GPU limits, asset streaming, background tasks and thermal behavior using frame-time evidence.

item.title: Does More RAM Actually Make Windows Faster? What to Measure Before Upgrading
item.description: More RAM can help when a workload is running short of memory, but the benefit depends on what Windows is doing before and after the upgrade.

item.title: How SSD Temperature Can Affect Real-World Performance
item.description: SSD temperature matters most when heat changes behavior. TWW explains how to distinguish harmless warmth from a thermal-performance problem.

item.title: Windows 11 26H2 Installation Guide: Upgrade, ISO and Fixes
item.description: Choose the right Windows 11 26H2 installation path, check compatibility, protect your files, verify official installation media, and troubleshoot setup problems safely.

item.title: Windows Says Connected but No Internet: Complete Troubleshooting Guide
item.description: How to tell whether a Windows PC with a Wi-Fi or Ethernet connection but no internet has a device, router, DNS, VPN, or service-provider problem, and what to test in what order.

item.title: Windows 11 DNS Not Working: How to Tell If DNS Is the Problem
item.description: How to recognize a DNS failure on Windows 11, tell it apart from a wider outage, and apply safe fixes without changing more than you need to.

item.title: Windows 11 Network Adapter Reset: When to Use It and What It Changes
item.description: What a Windows 11 network reset actually does, what you lose when you run it, and which checks should come first.

item.title: PC Game Stuttering: How to Diagnose Frame-Time Spikes, Microstutter & FPS Drops
item.description: A diagnostic guide to PC game stutter that separates frame-time spikes from low average FPS and works through shaders, CPU and GPU limits, memory, storage, drivers, and thermals.

item.title: GPU Frame-Time Spikes: Common Causes of Uneven PC Game Performance
item.description: How to tell whether frame-time spikes come from the GPU workload itself or from drivers, VRAM, thermals, and other parts of the system.

item.title: Shader Compilation Stutter in PC Games: Why It Happens and What to Check
item.description: Why many PC games hitch the first time effects appear, how shader caches change the behavior, and which checks separate shader stutter from other causes.

item.title: How to Check SSD Health in Windows
item.description: How to read SSD health information in Windows, what SMART values such as wear, spare capacity, and media errors mean, and when to back up and replace a drive.

item.title: NVMe SSD Temperature Too High: What Is Normal and When It Throttles
item.description: How to interpret NVMe SSD temperature readings, when heat reduces performance, and practical ways to improve cooling.

item.title: Why an SSD Can Slow Down Over Time: What to Check Before Replacing It
item.description: The most common reasons an SSD feels slower than before, from low free space and thermal throttling to background activity, drivers, and drive wear.

item.title: How to Check RAM for Errors on Windows (MemTest86 and Windows Memory Diagnostic)
item.description: How to tell whether random crashes, blue screens, or corrupted files point to faulty memory, which RAM test to run, and how to read the result.

item.title: Windows 11 Blue Screen Stop Codes: What They Mean and How to Find the Cause
item.description: A blue screen tells you what Windows detected, not always what is broken. Learn to read the stop code, find the crash record, and work from the cheapest test to the most invasive.

item.title: Windows 11 Freezing Randomly: How to Find the Cause
item.description: A freeze can come from a driver, a struggling drive, heat, memory, or power. Learn to classify the freeze, read the evidence Windows leaves behind, and test the likely causes in order.

item.title: Microsoft October 7 Windows & Surface Event: Surface Laptop Ultra, RTX Spark and Local AI
item.description: Microsoft has now shown its next Windows and Surface direction. Here is what was announced, what the new hardware means, and what matters for ordinary PC buyers.

item.title: Best SSDs for Gaming and Windows: How to Choose the Right Drive
item.description: A practical SSD buying guide covering PCIe generation, capacity, sustained performance, thermals, endurance, warranty and value without treating benchmark numbers as the whole story.

item.title: Best Gaming Laptops: How to Choose for Performance, Cooling and Value
item.description: A practical gaming-laptop buying guide that weighs GPU performance, CPU limits, cooling, display, memory, storage, battery behavior and upgradeability.

item.title: Best Gaming Monitors: How to Choose Resolution, Refresh Rate and Panel Behavior
item.description: How to choose a gaming monitor by resolution, refresh rate, response behavior, adaptive sync, panel characteristics and the GPU you actually own.

item.title: Best RAM for Gaming PCs and Windows: Capacity, Speed and Compatibility
item.description: A practical RAM buying guide covering capacity, memory speed, latency, dual-channel operation, XMP/EXPO, compatibility and upgrade planning.
